elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: Rendered: "except no such approval shall be required for an assignment by Client to an affiliate or successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets" — unconditional affiliate carve-out for Client (the prior "financially responsible" qualifier is subsumed in the rewritten Client-only exception).

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: Same carve-out expressly names "successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets" for Client, with no approval required.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: "Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights ... without the prior written approval of the other party" and the no-approval exception is now limited to "an assignment by Client", so TrueLink retains no unilateral exception (the former mutual affiliate exception was correctly narrowed).

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "without the prior written approval of the other party, not to be unreasonably withheld" — the reasonableness standard attaches to the approval requirement that governs TrueLink's assignments (and, mutually, Client's residual consents).

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: Second sentence: "TrueLink shall never assign or transfer its rights to a competitor of Client" — absolute bar, not subject to the consent mechanic.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: Second sentence: "a change of control of Client shall give TrueLink no right to terminate this Agreement"; no contrary change-of-control trigger exists elsewhere in the document, so no retained inconsistency.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: The no-approval exception runs only to "an assignment by Client"; TrueLink has no successor carve-out, so the right is one-sided rather than mutual.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: No notice mechanic appears in the rendered clause; the carve-out operates with no notification obligation.
A retained no-consent non-successor exception (Client transfers to an affiliate) survives, which under the stated boundary defeats this element at the fallback level.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "prior written approval of the other party, not to be unreasonably withheld" qualifies all approvals mutually.

reasons: All six preferred elements are met in operative language: the Client affiliate/successor no-approval carve-out, the mutual approval requirement retained against TrueLink, the reasonableness qualifier, the competitor bar, and the express statement that a Client change of control gives TrueLink no termination right.
The fallback level is not complete (one-sided successor right, no written-notice mechanic, retained Client affiliate exception), but that is immaterial because the preferred level is complete.

Minimality holds: the edit inserts one qualifying phrase, narrows the pre-existing exception to Client (necessary, since a retained mutual affiliate exception would defeat "Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent"), and adds one short sentence carrying only the two remaining checklist elements. No survival tails, procedures, or unrelated boilerplate were added.

Minor observation only (not a defect): the reasonableness standard is drafted mutually, so it also constrains Client's withholding of consent; this is the most concise placement and is consistent with the playbook's fallback formulation.

Intent is preserved: the mutual approval architecture, section numbering, and all unrelated commercial mechanics survive; no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created, and the change-of-control sentence contradicts nothing because the document contains no change-of-control trigger.

Deviation status is correct: the original clause failed the fallback on material terms (no successor/M&A carve-out for Client, no notice mechanic, unqualified approval standard) and its mutual "financially responsible affiliate" exception let TrueLink assign to affiliates without Client's approval.
